title: Projector driver definition
description: Declarative driver/capability definition. Data only -- there is no field anywhere in this schema that carries executable code. 'parse' is a string key into a fixed set of parser names implemented in Python; networking and parsing live in Python, never here. The DriverManager hand-rolls this same validation at load (no runtime dependency on a JSON-Schema library); this file is the human-readable contract.

driver_id.description: Unique id; the prefix names the tier and must match the folder it lives in.

extends.description: driver_id of the parent in the inheritance chain; must resolve to a loaded driver.

match.description: How a discovered device is matched to this driver. Omitted/empty never matches (except a protocol with always:true).

model_prefix.description: Family-level prefix match on the normalized model string.

pjlink_class.description: Required PJLink class (e.g. '1' or ['1','2']). A known-but-different class disqualifies; an unknown class neither helps nor hurts.

firmware_equals.description: Applied only when the device firmware is known.

command.description: Literal protocol command string sent on the wire. Data, not code.

parse.description: Name of a parser implemented in Python. The schema enumerates the allowed names; it carries no parsing logic.

confirm_with.description: Action to run after a command to refresh state (e.g. power.get).

transport.description: Per-capability transport override; otherwise the driver default (possibly inherited) is used.

meta.description: Provenance of this capability definition. Evidence itself lives in drivers/verification/, not here.

decoded.description: Honesty flag, e.g. 'unknown' when a returned code's meaning is not established by documentation.

source.description: Reference only -- never a copy of manufacturer documentation text.
